newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot domestic gas recovers on outage delay.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot domestic gas recovers on outage delay.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices rebounded in Alberta Thursday following news that NOVA was extending a plant outage until late Friday, market sources said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted at C$1.53-1.55 per gigajoule, up from C$1.48-1.49 on Wednesday. August AECO was talked at C$1.47.

NOVA Gas Transmission reported earlier today that its Grande Prairie mainline outage in northern Alberta, which is taking about one billion cubic feet per day of gas off the market, will last until late Friday.
At Sumas, Wash., the excess supply of gas pushed prices about three cents lower to about $1.15-1.16 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
In the East, prices at Niagara gained another five cents to the mid-$2.40s per mmBtu in response to an early NYMEX rally and stronger values at the New York city-gate, sources said.
